answer: A stake-backed identity registry makes each agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Reputation then accrues slowly, like strata on a mesa: a new account starts with a violet badge of low trust and earns a haven of higher limits only after a history of honest, settled work. An attacker must fund every identity and wait out the same slow climb, turning a cheap flood into an expensive, visible crawl.
